newsitem.title: GERMANY: Malta plane hijacked to Germany - police.
newsitem.headline: Malta plane hijacked to Germany - police.

text.p: An Air Malta plane with about 80 people on board was hijacked to Germany early on Monday on a flight from Malta to Istanbul, German police said.
The Boeing 737 airliner landed at Cologne-Bonn airport at 4.47 a.m. (0247 GMT) and was standing at a freight section of the busy airport.
Police established contact with what appeared to be a lone hijacker and said he had demanded a Turkish-speaking interpreter, indicating he was from Turkey or at least Turkish-speaking.
Maltese state-owned airline Air Malta said the situation on board the aircraft was "reported to be calm".
"Police have started a dialogue with the hijacker and I hope that will prove constructive," Heinz Gombel, chief executive of the airport, told reporters.
One woman was allowed to leave the plane because of heart problems.
The hijacker requested that a television crew come to the plane to act as mediators, Gombel said.

Air Malta spokesman John Saliba said the plane left Malta for Istanbul at 23.45GMT and was diverted to Cologne "following a situation that developed on board and demands made by one of the passengers."
Speaking in Valletta, he said he had no information yet on the hijacker's demands.
The Air Malta spokesman said there were 74 passengers and six crew on the Boeing 737. Most passengers on this flight were usually foreign, he said.
German police initially said there were 79 adults and one child and five crew on the airliner when it landed.
The hijacking was the first involving an Air Malta aircraft since the airline was formed in the early 1970s and the first hijack of a flight originating in Malta.
Air Malta has a growing network of services to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East including three weekly flights to Turkey.
